stem:
On a hot afternoon in her village in Rajasthan, Meena watches dark thunderstorm clouds build up over the heated fields. Her teacher asks her to explain how the heated land and the moist air above it produce a thunderstorm.
Which chain of events correctly explains the formation of the thunderstorm?

options.text: Rain clouds become heavy with water and simply fall down as rain.
Cool air sinks over the fields, creating high pressure that pushes the rain out of the clouds.
Moist air rises, cools and condenses into clouds, but no air flows in from surrounding areas.

The hot land warms the moist air above it; the warm air rises and creates a low-pressure region; cooler air flows in from surrounding high-pressure regions; the rising air cools and its water vapour condenses into clouds and rain.

teacher.key_rationale: A thunderstorm forms through the full pressure-driven circulation chain: surface heating warms moist air, the lighter air rises creating low pressure, cooler air flows in from surrounding high-pressure areas, and repeated rising, cooling and condensation builds storm clouds and rainfall. Only option D states this complete chain; A, B and C each omit or contradict essential steps.
